title: perf(tmux): replace repeated has-session/list-sessions polls with one control-mode watcher
description:
## .what

replace repeated `tmux has-session` / `list-sessions` calls from the duct and crew pollers with ONE long-lived tmux control-mode client that receives changes as events, and serves readers from its state.

## .why

- every `tmux <command>` from a poller forks a fresh tmux client, connects to the server socket, and parses a reply. at scale that is a churn source and a load on a single-threaded server
- measured on a dev box: one tmux server with ~190 sessions and ~156 attached clients. a 10s churn sample saw **~160 distinct short-lived `tmux` processes**, and a plain read query against the server took a visible fraction of a second to answer
- tmux control mode (wiki: Control Mode) is built for exactly this:
  - `tmux -C` starts a text-protocol client; it accepts ordinary commands and also emits async `%`-notifications when a change is made (`%sessions-changed`, `%session-changed`, `%window-add`, ...)
  - `refresh-client -B` adds a **format subscription**: tmux re-expands the format and sends `%subscription-changed` only when the value changes, **at most once a second**
  - `refresh-client -f no-output` stops `%output` notifications, so the watcher never pays for pane output

## .proposed shape

- one watcher per box holds the control-mode client and writes a cache (session list, per-session liveness, the formats readers need)
- readers (`duct.*`, `git.crew.*`, the pollers) read the cache instead of a fork per question
- the watcher restarts itself if the server restarts; readers fail loud on a stale cache rather than guess

## .acceptance

- a reader's question about session existence forks no tmux client
- measured before/after: distinct `tmux` processes per 10s sample, at the same session count

## .sources

- https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Control-Mode
- https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man1/tmux.1.html
